messages.subject: logistic regression
messages.body_plain:
hi,
I'm trying to understand if a categorical variable with about 40,000 possible values is effecting some ratio variable.
I want to see also the impact of each category.

I though of running logistic regresion:

model_1 = glm(formula = cbind(clicks, impressions-clicks) ~profile , data, family = binomial)

where profile has about 40K different string values.
but it seems like it is to heavy to handle.

eventually I would like to add more predicting variables (country for example..)
Can you think of a better way to solve the problem?

Thanks.

messages.subject: Re: logistic regression
messages.body_plain:
Do you wish to understand whether there is a significant effect, or try to predict the ratio variable?
How many samples do you have?

Essentially when you convert the categorical variable into binary (one hot encoding) you get 40,000 different features.
Now you can start doing feature selection or other dimensionality reduction techniques. You could also incorporate new features (country as you mentioned) at this point. This will better position you towards predicting the ratio variable.

If you wish to understand the effect, you can cluster categories (profiles) together and look for an effect at a higher granularity.

Hope this helps,
Omri

messages.subject: Re: Creating a data frame inside if statement
messages.subject_clean: Creating a data frame inside if statement
messages.body_plain:
You can't create a variable inside an if statement, and then use it outside, if the if was false.
A simple solution is to create this variable before the if statement, but without any initialization:

Qin <- data.frame(Qout = as.numeric(NULL), time = as.numeric(NULL))

This would give you a empty data frame, on which you can still call:

print(Qin$Qout)

messages.subject: TSstudio - New R Package for Time Series Analysis
messages.subject_clean: TSstudio - New R Package for Time Series Analysis
messages.body_plain:
Hello all!

Wanted to introduce you the TSstudio package for time series analysis. It provides a set of interactive visualization tools (which based on the plotly visualization engine)  for time series analysis supporting ts, mts, zoo and xts objects along some of the outputs of the forecast package. First version available on CRAN or Github.

For more information:
Package Vignette - https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/TSstudio/vignettes/TSstudio_Intro.html

Github page - https://github.com/RamiKrispin/TSstudio

Thanks,
Rami
